header:
Why the same flight
costs different amounts

lines.text: Your seatmate paid $150. You paid $400. Same seat.
lines.say: Your seatmate paid a hundred fifty. You paid four hundred. Same seat.

lines.text: Airlines split each cabin into fare buckets, with letter codes like Y, B and M.
lines.say: Airlines split each cabin into fare buckets, with letter codes like Y, B and M.

lines.text: When the cheapest bucket sells out, it closes and a pricier one opens.
lines.say: When the cheapest bucket sells out, it closes, and a pricier one opens.

lines.text: Example: 150 seats, fifty each at $150, $250 and $400, bring in $40,000.
lines.say: Say fifty seats sell at one fifty, fifty at two hundred fifty, and fifty at four hundred. That's forty thousand dollars.

lines.text: Sell them all at $150 and it's just $22,500.
lines.say: Sell them all at a hundred fifty, and it's twenty-two thousand five hundred.

lines.text: In 2025, Delta's premium tickets brought in $22.1 billion, close to main cabin's $23.4 billion.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, Delta's premium tickets brought in twenty-two point one billion dollars, close to main cabin's twenty-three point four billion.

lines.text: And its American Express card deal paid Delta $8.2 billion in 2025.
lines.say: And its American Express card deal paid Delta eight point two billion dollars in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Meanwhile, the average domestic fare, adjusted for inflation, fell from $618 in 1995 to $387 in 2025.
lines.say: Meanwhile, the average domestic fare, adjusted for inflation, fell from about six hundred twenty dollars in nineteen ninety-five to about three ninety in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Takeaway: you're paying for which bucket was open, not a better seat.
lines.say: The takeaway? You're paying for which bucket was open, not a better seat.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Why the same flight costs different amounts
post.ig:
Your seatmate paid $150. You paid $400. Same seat.

Airlines split each cabin into fare buckets. When the cheap one sells out, a pricier one opens.
In 2025, Delta's premium tickets brought in $22.1B vs $23.4B for main cabin, and Amex paid Delta $8.2B.
The average US domestic fare, inflation-adjusted, fell from $618 in 1995 to $387 in 2025.

Sources: Delta 2025 Form 10-K, BTS (Apr 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.

post.yt_desc:
Airlines split each cabin into fare buckets, and when the cheapest one sells out a pricier one opens, so the same seat can cost very different amounts. In 2025 Delta's premium tickets brought in $22.1 billion and American Express paid it $8.2 billion (Delta 2025 10-K); the average US domestic fare fell to $387 in 2025 (BTS, inflation-adjusted).

News and education, not financial advice.
